name: Mental Maths: Fast Multiplication — 5, 25, 50 & 125
description: KaTeX-enabled multiplication practice for the high-value factors 5, 25, 50, and 125. It teaches exact transformations, splitting for awkward inputs, factor pairing, powers-of-ten anchors, estimation, and method selection.
estimatedTime: 140–180 minutes for a first focused pass; then 10–15 minute review bursts

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: Why are 5, 25, 50, and 125 special?
Fast Multiplication: How do you multiply by 5?
cards.definition:
Multiply by 10, then halve.

$$
\begin{aligned}
74\times5 \\
&=740\div2 \\
&=370
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: How do you multiply by 25?
cards.definition:
When the other factor is divisible by 4, divide it by 4 and multiply by 100.

$$
\begin{aligned}
64\times25 \\
&=16\times100 \\
&=1600
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: How do you multiply by 50?
cards.definition:
When the other factor is even, divide it by 2 and multiply by 100.

$$
\begin{aligned}
46\times50 \\
&=23\times100 \\
&=2300
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: How do you multiply by 125?
cards.definition:
When the other factor is divisible by 8, divide it by 8 and multiply by 1000.

$$
\begin{aligned}
72\times125 \\
&=9\times1000 \\
&=9000
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: What if a × 25 factor is not divisible by 4?
cards.definition:
Split into a nearby multiple of 4 plus the remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned}
38\times25 \\
&=(36+2)\times25 \\
&=900+50 \\
&=950
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: What if a × 125 factor is not divisible by 8?
cards.definition:
Split or factor to create an 8.

$$
\begin{aligned}
48\times125 \\
&=6\times(8\times125) \\
&=6000
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: Why does double-and-half work?
cards.definition:
Doubling one factor while halving the other preserves the product.

$$
\begin{aligned}
24\times125 \\
&=12\times250 \\
&=6\times500 \\
&=3\times1000 \\
&=3000
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: When should you not force a special-factor trick?
cards.definition: When splitting is cleaner. For 43 × 25, use 40 × 25 + 3 × 25 = 1000 + 75 = 1075.

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: Which method is best for 56 × 125?
cards.definition:
Pair the hidden 8 with 125.

$$
\begin{aligned}
56\times125 \\
&=7\times1000 \\
&=7000
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: Which method is best for 37 × 50?
cards.definition:
Use 50 = 5 × 10.

$$
\begin{aligned}
37\times50 \\
&=185\times10 \\
&=1850
\end{aligned}
$$

cards.term: Fast Multiplication: How do you estimate these products?
cards.definition: 73 × 125 is close to 72 × 125 = 9000, so the exact value should be slightly above 9000. It is 9125.

True or false: n × 25 = n ÷ 4 × 100 is clean using integers for every n.
cards.definition: False. It is clean only when n is divisible by 4. Otherwise split or use a different route.

cards.term: True or false: n × 125 = n ÷ 8 × 1000 is clean using integers for every n.
cards.definition: False. It is clean only when n is divisible by 8.
No. Since 84 contains a factor of 4, 84 × 25 is a multiple of 100. Exact answer: 2100.
